name: Massachusetts utility shutoff protections (220 CMR 25.00)

applies_to.citation: 220 CMR 25.01(1): applies to DPU-regulated gas, electric and water companies and all municipal gas and electric departments, corporations and plants

financial_hardship.definition: Customer is unable to pay an overdue bill AND meets income eligibility for the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (HEAP), or the DPU Consumer Division finds hardship is warranted.
ways_to_show: Return the utility's financial hardship form within 7 days of receiving it
A signed statement that income is within HEAP guidelines counts as presumptive evidence
Utility received HEAP payments for the customer last winter (see prior_winter_heap_presumption)
financial_hardship.renewal: Hardship form renewed quarterly; renewal waived for the winter period if hardship is ongoing

protections.name: Winter shutoff protection (Winter Moratorium)
conditions: Service provides heat or runs the heating system
Service was not shut off for nonpayment before the moratorium start date
script_must_include: Ask the utility for winter protection
Ask for the financial hardship form and return it within 7 days

protections.name: You may already be protected if you got HEAP last winter
conditions: Utility received fuel assistance payments for this customer in the prior winter
protections.effect: Utility must presume financial hardship and protect the account from the moratorium start date through January 1, so the customer has time to apply for HEAP this winter. If the customer has not applied or certified hardship by January 1, normal collection may resume.
protections.action_reason: Protection ends January 1 unless the household applies for HEAP or certifies hardship. The household should also call to confirm the utility has them on record.
script_must_include: Call to confirm you are protected

protections.name: Infant protection
conditions: A child under 12 months old lives in the home

certification.initial: Can start with a phone call to the utility
accepted_documents: Letter or official document from a physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, local board of health, hospital, government official, Department of Transitional Assistance, clergy, or religious institution
certification.must_state: Child's name, birthdate and home address
certification.renewal: None until the child turns 12 months

protections.name: Serious illness protection
conditions: The customer or someone in the home is seriously ill

certification.initial: A physician, physician assistant, nurse practitioner, or local board of health official must call the utility
certification.certificate_must_state: Ill person's name and address, the nature of the illness, and the certifier's business address and phone
certification.renewal: Every 3 months; every 6 months if certified as chronic

protections.name: Protection for homes where all adults are 65+ and a child lives there
conditions: All adults in the home are 65 or older
A minor lives in the home

protections.name: Protection for homes where everyone is 65+
conditions: Every person living in the home is 65 or older
protections.effect: The utility cannot shut off service for an unpaid bill without written approval from the DPU, and the household has a right to a DPU hearing first.
protections.action_reason: The utility must know that all residents are 65+. Tell the utility, and consider naming a third person to receive copies of shutoff notices.

extras.third_party_notice: A customer 65+ can name someone to get copies of past-due and shutoff notices; that person is not responsible for the bill

rights_during_any_shutoff.text: If a utility worker comes to shut off service and someone at home claims a protection, the shutoff must be postponed 72 hours to allow time to get certification.
If the utility says you don't qualify for protection and you dispute it, the utility cannot shut off service while the dispute is pending. You have 7 days to contact the DPU.
During the winter period, the utility must call or visit heating customers no earlier than 3 days before a shutoff.
During the winter period, the utility may not send shutoff-threat notices to a customer who has given notice of financial hardship.
Shutoffs for nonpayment can only happen 8 AM to 4 PM, Monday to Thursday, and not on a holiday or the day before one.
Every utility must offer payment plans and budget plans.

dpu_consumer_division.status: VERIFY current number on mass.gov; the regulation text is from 2012 and lists two different numbers in 25.02(4) and 25.05(5)

notes: Every protection has requires_action = true. Heat Path never says a household is protected with no action needed. Tenant protections when a landlord doesn't pay (220 CMR 25.04) are out of scope for this version.
